name: Battle of Demotika
commanders: Ottoman forces supporting John VI Kantakouzenos; Serbian-Bulgarian allied forces
result: First major Ottoman victory in Europe
importance: Opened the way for a permanent Ottoman military role in Thrace.

name: Battle of Kulikovo
commanders: Dmitry Donskoy vs. Mamai
importance: Established Moscow as the primary political center for anti-Horde resistance and broke the aura of Tatar invincibility.
casualties: Very heavy losses on both sides.

name: Great Stand on the Ugra River
commanders: Ivan III vs. Akhmat Khan
importance: Formally terminated two and a half centuries of Tatar tribute and suzerainty over Russian principalities.

name: First Battle of Vajkal
commanders: Skanderbeg vs. Ballaban Pasha
importance: Fought in the Vajkal valley; Skanderbeg's forces defeated Ballaban Pasha's Ottoman army, though heavy losses were sustained on both sides and several prominent Albanian officers were captured during an overzealous pursuit and later executed in Constantinople
casualties: Heavy casualties on both sides; several captured Albanian commanders skinned alive

name: Second Battle of Vajkal
commanders: Skanderbeg vs. Ballaban Pasha
importance: Fought in August 1465 following Ballaban's renewed invasion; an Albanian army of 12,000 men under Skanderbeg utterly defeated a 24,000-strong Ottoman army led by Ballaban Pasha

name: Battle of Otlukbeli
commanders: Mehmed the Conqueror, Prince Bayezid & Prince Mustafa vs. Uzun Hasan (Aq Qoyunlu)
importance: Fought near Tercan/Otlukbeli; Mehmed II's massive Ottoman army decisively defeated Uzun Hasan's Aq Qoyunlu forces, neutralizing the major Eastern threat to Ottoman rule in Anatolia and breaking Aq Qoyunlu regional dominance
casualties: Heavy Aq Qoyunlu casualties, including the death of Zeynel Mirza and the capture of high-ranking commanders

name: Battle of Lipnic
commanders: Stephen the Great vs. Ahmed Khan (Golden Horde)
importance: Repelled a major Volga-Tatar invasion of Moldavia, capturing Ahmed Khan's son and strengthening Moldavian sovereignty.
casualties: Heavy Tatar losses; capture of numerous prisoners.

name: Sack of Sarai
commanders: Crimean Khanate (Mengli I Giray) vs. Great Horde (Sheikh Ahmad)
importance: Destroyed the capital of the Great Horde, permanently extinguishing its statehood and dividing its remnants among rival khanates.
casualties: Heavy devastation of the city and surrounding nomadic forces.

name: Battle of the Samara River
commanders: Stephen III & Meñli I Giray vs. Sheikh Ahmed
importance: Catastrophic blow leading to the destruction of the Golden Horde
casualties: Most of the Great Horde army destroyed

name: Battle of the Cosmin Forest
commanders: Stephen III (Moldavia, Wallachia, Ottoman Empire, Crimean Khanate) vs. King John I Albert
importance: Disastrous defeat for Poland, ending King John's attempt to subjugate Moldavia

name: Battle of Kopystrzyń
commanders: Prince John I Albert vs. Tatar Chambul
importance: Defeat of an Ottoman-dispatched Tatar raiding force in Podolia
casualties: Approx. 1,500 to 2,000 Tatars killed or captured

name: Battle of Zasław
commanders: Mikołaj Chodecki & Semyon Olshanski vs. Crimean Khanate
importance: Near-total destruction of a 9,000-strong Crimean raiding force along the Horyn River

name: Battle of Ștefănești
commanders: Stephen III vs. Eminek Mârza
importance: Repelled a diversionary Crimean-Nogai Tatar invasion of northern Moldavia ordered by Sultan Mehmed II
casualties: Very heavy losses for the Tatar forces

name: Battle of Cernăuți
commanders: Stephen III & Sima Boldur vs. King John I Albert & Konrad III Rudy
importance: An ambush on retreating Polish forces crossing the Prut River, completing the devastation of John I Albert's army
casualties: Very heavy losses, finishing the decimation of the Polish expedition

name: Battle of Lențești
commanders: Sima Boldur (trusted by Stephen III) vs. Konrad III Rudy
importance: An annihilation of 600 Masovian knights sent to relieve the retreating Polish army
casualties: All Masovian knights killed / completely wiped out

name: Sacking of Trembowla
commanders: Stephen III vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Captured and sacked as part of Stephen's retaliatory invasion of southeastern Poland

name: Sacking of Buczacz
commanders: Stephen III vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Captured and pillaged during the 1498 Moldavian campaign in Red Ruthenia

name: Sacking of Podhajce
commanders: Stephen III vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Fell to Stephen's advancing forces during the sweeping punitive raids into Poland

name: Moldavian Punitive Campaign in Poland
commanders: Stephen III (with Ottoman & Crimean allies) vs. King John I Albert
importance: Widespread devastation of Red Ruthenia and Podolia up to Lwów, Przemyśl, and Jarosław, forcing a Polish peace treaty
casualties: Enormous devastation; up to 100,000 Polish captives taken

name: Raid on Lwów
commanders: Stephen III vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Stephen's army ravaged the lands up to the major regional center of Lwów

name: Campaign in Pokucie
commanders: Stephen III vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Systematic devastation and foraging across the Pokucie region over the Dniester

name: Raid on Przemyśl
commanders: Stephen III vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Deep punitive raid reaching and devastating the city and environs of Przemyśl

name: Sacking of Radymno
commanders: Stephen III vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Town sacked and burned during the retaliatory sweep through southeastern Poland

name: Sacking of Jarosław
commanders: Stephen III vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Major urban center of Jarosław ravaged by Stephen's advancing coalition forces
casualties: City and surrounding lands heavily plundered

name: Pillaging of Kańczuga
commanders: Stephen III vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Locality pillaged during the wide-ranging Moldavian offensive

name: Destruction of Łańcut
commanders: Stephen III vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Town and estate lands of Łańcut devastated before the Polish army could mobilize at Sandomierz

name: Zhane–Elbrus Campaign
commanders: Sahib I Giray & Khalil Bey vs. Kansavuk (Zhane)
importance: First major expedition into Circassia, reaching Mount Tkhab and the upper Kuban region

name: Zhane Campaign
commanders: Sahib I Giray & Khalil Bey vs. Kansavuk (Zhane)
importance: Punitive expedition against Zhane lands following refusal to pay tribute and Taman raids
casualties: Widespread devastation; ~50,000 civilians captured over 75 days

name: Campaign to Kabardia
commanders: Sahib I Giray vs. Kabardian and Bzhedug Princes
importance: Major clash along the Malka and Belkh rivers involving an army of up to 70,000 Tatars

name: Astrakhan Conflict & Storming
commanders: Sahib I Giray vs. Yamghurchi Khan
importance: Massive mobilization and storming of Astrakhan, devastating the Astrakhan Khanate and deporting Nogais

name: Hatuqay Campaign
commanders: Sahib I Giray & Ghazi Giray vs. Elok & Antanuk (Hatuqay/Bzhedug)
importance: Final major campaign of Sahib Giray into Hatuqay and the foothills of Elbrus before his assassination

name: Battle of Buzhyn
commanders: Grigory Romodanovsky & Ivan Samoilovich vs. Ibrahim Pasha & Selim I Giray
importance: Forced the Ottoman army to lift the siege of Chyhyryn and retreat, securing victory in the 1677 campaign

name: Battle of the Alma
commanders: Mykhailo Doroshenko & Shahin Giray vs. Khan Temir & Ottoman Janissaries
importance: Cossack forces defeated Khan Temir's army to lift the siege of Bakhchysarai
casualties: 100–1,000 Cossacks killed (including Hetman Doroshenko); ~200 Nogai/Ottoman troops killed

name: Battle of the Tyzyl Gorge (Kanzhal Campaign)
commanders: Kurghoqo Hatokhshoqo vs. Qaplan I Giray
importance: Initial guerrilla phase where Kabardian forces trapped and decimated Crimean detachments in narrow gorges using rolling stones and archers
casualties: Heavy losses for the invading Tatar forces

name: Battle of Kanzhal
commanders: Kurghoqo Hatokhshoqo & Jabagh Qazanoqo vs. Qaplan I Giray
importance: Night surprise attack utilizing fire-driven panic, virtually destroying the Crimean-Ottoman army and shattering Khanate influence in the region
casualties: 30,000–40,000 Crimean/Ottoman casualties; Khan Qaplan I Giray barely escapes

name: Battle of the Afips River
commanders: Adil Giray & Devlet I Giray vs. Temruqo Idar & Western Circassians
importance: Fierce engagement along the Afips river where the famous Kabardian leader Temruqo Idar was mortally wounded
casualties: Very heavy losses on both sides; multiple Circassian nobles killed or captured

name: Moldavian Campaign in Red Ruthenia
commanders: Stephen III (with Ottoman and Crimean allies) vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Systematic devastation and slaving raids across the Red Ruthenia region up to Lwów
casualties: Heavy regional devastation and mass enslavement

name: Moldavian Campaign in Podolia
commanders: Stephen III (with Ottoman and Crimean allies) vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Comprehensive pillaging and destruction across Podolian lands during the punitive expedition

name: Advance to Przeworsk (1498 Campaign)
commanders: Stephen III (with Ottoman & Crimean allies) vs. Kingdom of Poland
importance: Deep invasion following the crossing of the Dniestr, ransacking Red Ruthenia and reaching as far as Przeworsk
casualties: Massive devastation and up to 100,000 people taken captive

name: Construction of the Kraków Barbican
commanders: King John I Albert
importance: Built in haste following the disastrous Moldavian campaign and fear of an Ottoman retaliatory invasion on Kraków

name: Battle of Fenesu Mare (Death of Rákóczi)
commanders: George II Rákóczi vs. Ottoman-backed forces
importance: Rákóczi was mortally wounded in this battle and died shortly after, marking the definitive end of his reign and Transylvania's independent ambitions
casualties: George II Rákóczi mortally wounded, died shortly afterward

name: Ottoman-Tatar Punitive Invasion of Transylvania
commanders: Ottoman/Crimean Tatar forces (Sultan-ordered) vs. George II Rákóczi
importance: Retaliation for Rákóczi's unauthorized 1657 campaign; devastated Transylvania and began the Porte's direct reassertion of control over the principality
casualties: Widespread devastation of Transylvanian towns and countryside

name: Capitulation of Rákóczi's Army
commanders: George II Rákóczi vs. Crimean Tatar forces
importance: Isolated and surrounded during retreat, Rákóczi's remaining forces were forced to capitulate to the Tatars, effectively ending the Polish campaign in disaster
casualties: Large portions of the Transylvanian army killed or taken captive

name: Battle of Kassa
commanders: Aeneas de Caprara vs. Abdi Pasha the Albanian
importance: Regained Habsburg control over Upper Hungary / Košice, which had been lost to Imre Thököly's Kuruc forces in 1682.

name: Siege of Santa Maura
commanders: Francesco Morosini vs. Bekir Agha
importance: The opening battle of the Sixth Ottoman–Venetian (Morean) War; a Venetian fleet and land force under Francesco Morosini successfully besieged and captured the strategic fortress of Santa Maura on Lefkada after intensive bombardment and a negotiated surrender
casualties: 127 Venetians killed, 128 wounded, and heavy losses due to disease; 700 garrison members and 3,000 civilians evacuated safely

name: Siege of Virovitica
commanders: James Leslie & Trautmansdorf vs. Ottoman garrison
importance: An early major success of the Great Turkish War in the Croatian–Slavonian theater; allied Habsburg and Croatian forces under James Leslie besieged and captured the strategic Ottoman border town of Virovitica after intercepting a relief force and negotiating a surrender, establishing a vital base for future operations in Slavonia
casualties: Garrison and relief force losses; Ottoman forces captured alive during interception

name: Conquest of Coron
commanders: Francesco Morosini vs. Halil Pasha
importance: The opening campaign of the Venetian conquest of the Morea during the Great Turkish War; a Venetian-led allied force successfully besieged and captured the strategic Ottoman fortress of Coron after defeating an Ottoman relief army and breaching the citadel walls
casualties: Garrison massacred following an accidental explosion during surrender negotiations; over 1,336 inhabitants enslaved; unknown Venetian/allied casualties

name: Battle of Kalamata
commanders: Hannibal von Degenfeld & Maximilian William of Brunswick-Lüneburg vs. Kapudan Pasha
importance: Fought during the Morean War; an allied Venetian expeditionary army under Hannibal von Degenfeld attacked and routed an entrenched Ottoman force outside Kalamata, cementing the Venetian foothold in the southern Morea, prompting the destruction of the obsolete local castle, and completing the liberation of the Mani Peninsula
casualties: Heavy Ottoman casualties and retreat; minor Venetian-allied losses

name: Battle of Mani
commanders: Francesco Morosini, Hannibal von Degenfeld & Pavlos Makris vs. Ismail Pasha & Kapudan Pasha
importance: A key phase of the Morean War where Venetian victories at Coron and Kalamata, combined with renewed Maniot uprisings, forced the capitulation and evacuation of Ottoman garrisons from Zarnata, Kelefa, and Passavas, securing the Mani Peninsula for Venice
casualties: Heavy Ottoman garrison evacuations and losses; allied losses from combat and winter disease

name: Battle of Cape Corvo
commanders: Ottavio d'Aragona vs. Sinari Pasha
importance: A major naval engagement of the Ottoman-Habsburg wars near Samos; a Sicilian-Spanish squadron under Ottavio d'Aragona ambushed and defeated an Ottoman fleet, capturing seven galleys and around 600 prisoners, marking the greatest Spanish naval victory over the Ottomans since Lepanto
casualties: 6 Spaniards killed, 30 wounded; ~400 Ottomans killed, 600 captured, and 1,200 Christian galley slaves freed

name: Battle on Vrtijeljka
commanders: Bošković, Bajo Pivljanin & Antonio Zeno vs. Süleyman Pasha of Scutari
importance: Fought on the hill of Vrtijeljka near Cetinje at the start of the Morean War; an Ottoman force under Süleyman Pasha of Scutari defeated a Venetian irregular force and Montenegrin-Hajduk fighters, resulting in the death of the famed hajduk leader Bajo Pivljanin and the display of severed heads in Constantinople
casualties: Heavy Christian and Hajduk casualties, including the death of Bajo Pivljanin and dozens of fighters; significant Ottoman losses

name: Battle of Párkány
commanders: John III Sobieski and Charles V, Duke of Lorraine vs. Ottoman field army
importance: Crushed the retreating Ottoman forces in northern Hungary immediately after the relief of Vienna.
casualties: Heavy for Ottomans, light for Christians

name: Rákóczi's Invasion of Poland (Treaty of Radnot Campaign)
commanders: George II Rákóczi & Antin Zhdanovych (Cossacks) & Swedish allies vs. Polish-Lithuanian forces
importance: Unauthorized invasion of Poland under the Treaty of Radnot, launched without Ottoman consent, in alliance with Charles X Gustav of Sweden and Khmelnytsky's Cossacks; part of the broader 'Deluge'

name: Abandonment by Sweden and Cossack Withdrawal
commanders: George II Rákóczi vs. Polish-Lithuanian forces & Crimean Tatars
importance: Charles X Gustav withdrew to counter a Danish threat, leaving Rákóczi's army isolated; Cossack support also withdrew, exposing Transylvanian forces to encirclement

name: Battle of Lubieszów
commanders: Jan Zborowski vs. Johann Winkelbruch
importance: A smaller royal army (~2,500 men) decisively defeated a much larger Danzig-mercenary army (~10,000–12,000 men), leading into the Siege of Danzig
casualties: 4,416–4,427 Danzig soldiers killed and 1,000–5,000 captured vs. 58 killed and 127 wounded for the Commonwealth

name: Siege of Vác
commanders: Charles V, Duke of Lorraine vs. Ottoman-Kuruc outposts
importance: Cleared opposing Ottoman-Kuruc strongholds along the Danube valley during maneuvers leading to Buda.

name: Battle of Eperjes
commanders: General Schulz vs. Imre Thököly
importance: Fought near Eperjes (Prešov, Slovakia) during the Great Turkish War; Imperial Habsburg forces under General Schulz decisively defeated the anti-Habsburg Kuruc and Ottoman allied forces led by Imre Thököly
casualties: Unspecified losses; decisive defeat for Thököly's forces

name: First Siege of Esztergom
commanders: John III Sobieski and Charles V, Duke of Lorraine vs. Ottoman garrison
importance: Recaptured the strategic fortress city of Esztergom following the success at Párkány.

name: Fall of Kazan
commanders: Ivan the Terrible vs. Khan Yadegar Mokhammad
importance: The fall of the Kazan Khanate shattered the Turkic-Islamic balance in the middle Volga region and marked the beginning of Russian expansion into the Kipchak steppes.

name: Capture of Aden and Red Sea Campaign
commanders: Hadim Suleiman Pasha vs. Local Yemeni Rulers / Portuguese forces
importance: Secured Aden and the choke point of the southern Red Sea against Portuguese naval hegemony, establishing the Ottoman Eyalet of Yemen.

name: Siege of Jeddah
commanders: Ottoman garrison vs. Portuguese fleet under Estêvão da Gama
importance: Repulsed a major Portuguese expedition aimed at destroying Islamic holy sites and cutting off Ottoman maritime trade in the Red Sea.

name: Battle of Tlemcen / Campaigns in North Africa
commanders: Salah Reis vs. Saadi / Local rivals
importance: Solidified Ottoman-Barbary control across the North African littoral, countering Spanish and local dynastic opposition.

name: War of Parma
commanders: Ottavio Farnese, Henry II of France vs. Charles V, Pope Julius III
importance: Opened the Italian War of 1551–1559 over control of Parma and French influence in northern Italy.

name: Invasion of Gozo
commanders: Ottoman navy vs. Knights of Malta
importance: Preceded the conquest of Tripoli by weeks

name: Ottoman-Adal Campaign against Abyssinia
commanders: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi (supported by Ottoman musketeers) vs. Ethiopian-Portuguese forces
importance: Marked the high-water mark and subsequent check of Muslim-Ottoman aligned expansion in the Horn of Africa and the southern Red Sea basin.

name: Siege / Blockade of Kamianets
commanders: Jan III Sobieski / Stanisław Jan Jabłonowski vs. Ottoman Garrison
importance: Repeated Polish attempts to blockade and starve out the major Ottoman fortress wedge in Podolia following the victory at Vienna, which ultimately held out until the 1699 Treaty of Karlowitz.

name: Skirmishes of Göllersdorf and the Austrian Marches
commanders: Habsburg border garrisons vs. Ottoman Akinji raiders
importance: Represented the penetration of Ottoman raiding parties deep into Lower Austria along the Morava and Danube river valleys, checked by Habsburg border defense forces.

name: Siege of Buda
commanders: Charles V, Duke of Lorraine vs. Ottoman garrison
importance: The massive Habsburg attempt to capture the vital Ottoman stronghold of Buda failed due to stubborn garrison defense and winter conditions.

name: Siege around Érsekújvár
commanders: Habsburg Imperial forces vs. Ottoman garrison
importance: Targeted operations and blockades to isolate key Ottoman regional strongholds in upper Hungary.

name: Battle of Vezekény
commanders: Ádám Forgách and Ladislaus Esterházy vs. Bey Mustafa
importance: A notable 17th-century engagement where Hungarian forces secured a victory against Ottoman raiders, though at the cost of notable noble leaders of the Esterházy family.

name: Capture of Gallipoli
commanders: Suleyman Pasha; Byzantine local defenders
importance: Established the first durable Ottoman base on the European side of the Dardanelles.

name: Battle of Jiliște
commanders: John III the Terrible & Ivan Svirhovsky vs. Sokollu Mehmed Pasha, Peter the Lame & Alexander II Mircea
importance: Major Moldavian-Cossack victory during the Moldavian campaign of 1574 against combined Ottoman, Crimean, and Wallachian forces.
casualties: Heavy Ottoman-Crimean losses; entire enemy force routed.

name: Battle of Cătlăbuga
commanders: Stephen III of Moldavia & Jan Karnkowski vs. Ottoman forces
importance: Moldavian-Polish victory near Chilia during the Moldavian campaign of 1484–1486, though Stephen ultimately ceased attempts to retake Chilia.

name: Battle of Dubica
commanders: Petar Berislavić, Nikola III Zrinski & Mihovil Frankopan vs. Junuz-aga (Ottoman forces)
importance: Fought near Dubica between the Sava and Una rivers; a Croatian army under Ban Petar Berislavić decisively defeated an Ottoman raiding force from the Sanjak of Bosnia, inflicting heavy losses and freeing numerous Christian captives
casualties: Heavy Ottoman casualties (estimated between 2,000 and 7,000 killed, drowned, or captured, including several commanders)

name: Battle of Plješevica
commanders: Petar Berislavić vs. Ottoman Empire forces
importance: An engagement on Mount Plješevica during which the veteran Croatian Ban Petar Berislavić was ambushed and killed after years of relentless campaigning against Ottoman incursions
casualties: Croatian forces defeated; death of Ban Petar Berislavić

name: Battle of Botoșani
commanders: Stephen III of Moldavia vs. Bayezid II
importance: Major Moldavian victory during the Moldavian-Ottoman War (1498–1500), resulting in a disastrous rout of the Ottoman army.

name: Battle of Ștefănești
commanders: Stephen III of Moldavia vs. Eminek Mârza
importance: Moldavian victory during the Moldavian-Ottoman War (1475–1476) against invading Crimean-Nogai Tatar forces.

name: Battle of Cahul
commanders: John the Terrible & Ivan Svirhovsky vs. Ottoman-Crimean forces
importance: Decisive suppression of the Moldavian Revolt following noble betrayal; resulted in the execution of Prince John the Terrible and the capture of Cossack hetman Ivan Svirhovsky.

name: Capture of Yazlovets
commanders: Jan III Sobieski vs. Ottoman garrison
importance: Marked the opening success of the first phase of the Moldavian campaign.

name: Battle of Boiany
commanders: Stanisław Jan Jabłonowski vs. Sulieman Pasha, Constantin Cantemir, and Crimean forces
importance: Defeated the invading Polish army in Bukovina, forcing a grueling retreat and stalling Polish expansion aims.

name: Skirmish at Bukovina Forest
commanders: Stanisław Jan Jabłonowski vs. Ottoman and Crimean pursuers
result: Indecisive tactical engagement / Strategic Ottoman pursuit
importance: A fierce rearguard action during the retreat back across the Prut River, successfully protecting the remnants of the Polish army.

name: Capture of Adrianople (Edirne)
commanders: Murad I and Lala Sahin Pasha; Byzantine defenders
importance: Gave the Ottomans a major Thracian capital and road hub.

name: Battle of Maritsa (Sirpsindigi)
commanders: Ottoman raiding forces; Balkan coalition
importance: Early victory consolidating Ottoman power in Thrace.

name: Adrianople officially becomes capital
commanders: Murad I
importance: Marked the European orientation of the expanding Ottoman state.

name: Capture of Serres
commanders: Ottoman Rumelian forces; Byzantine/Serbian local defenders
importance: Strengthened Ottoman control of eastern Macedonia.

name: Capture of Sofia
commanders: Lala Sahin Pasha; Bulgarian defenders
importance: Secured a key road junction into the western Balkans.

name: Capture of Nis
commanders: Murad I; Serbian defenders
importance: Opened the Morava corridor toward Serbia.

name: Capture of Thessaloniki (temporary)
commanders: Ottoman Rumelian forces; Byzantine defenders
importance: First Ottoman occupation of the major Aegean port before its later permanent conquest.

name: Campaign into Bosnia
commanders: Ottoman frontier commanders; Bosnian forces
importance: Extended Ottoman pressure into Bosnia before later conquest.

name: Battle of Kosovo
commanders: Murad I; Prince Lazar
importance: Reshaped Serbian-Ottoman relations and Balkan power politics.

name: Capture of Skopje
commanders: Pasa Yigit Bey; Serbian local authorities
importance: Made Skopje a major Ottoman base in the Vardar corridor.

name: Siege of Tarnovo
commanders: Ottoman forces; Bulgarian defenders
importance: Crippled the Second Bulgarian Empire.

name: Battle of Rovine
commanders: Bayezid I; Mircea the Elder
importance: Demonstrated the contested nature of Ottoman suzerainty over Wallachia.

name: Battle of Nicopolis
commanders: Bayezid I; Sigismund of Hungary
importance: Destroyed a major anti-Ottoman crusade on the Danube.

name: Sack of Patras (Spanish)
commanders: Spanish Fleet vs. Ottoman Garrison
importance: Part of anti-Ottoman naval operations; the city was significantly damaged by fire.

name: Pillage of Patras (Maltese)
commanders: Knights of Malta vs. Ottoman Garrison
importance: A destructive naval raid highlighting the vulnerability of Peloponnesian coastal cities.

name: Raid of Moravia
commanders: Ottoman and Crimean Tatar forces; Habsburg forces
importance: A major tactical raid disrupting Habsburg supply lines during the Austro-Turkish War.
casualties: Significant disruption and material losses in the Moravian region.

name: Siege of Ioannina
commanders: Ottoman forces; Byzantine/local defenders
importance: The surrender of Ioannina marked a significant step in the Ottoman consolidation of Epirus.

name: Battle of Romhány
commanders: Habsburg vs. Ottoman Empire
importance: An early engagement of the Long Turkish War on the northern Hungarian front.

name: Battle of Guruslău
commanders: Michael the Brave and Giorgio Basta vs. Mózes Székely
importance: One of the final major military successes for Michael the Brave in Transylvania.

name: Battle of Humenné
commanders: Walenty Rogawski & George Drugeth vs. George Rákóczi
importance: Polish-Habsburg allied forces under Walenty Rogawski defeated George Rákóczi's Transylvanian corps, forcing Gábor Bethlen to lift the siege of Vienna and retreat
casualties: Heavy losses for Transylvanians during the unexpected counterattack

name: Siege of Stuhlweissenburg (1601)
commanders: Habsburg forces vs. Ottoman garrison
importance: The strategic fortress was briefly recaptured by Christian forces.

name: Siege of Székesfehérvár (1602)
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg forces
importance: The Ottomans successfully reclaimed this critical stronghold.

name: Battle of Brașov
commanders: Radu Șerban vs. Mózes Székely
importance: The defeat and death of the Transylvanian prince Mózes Székely.

name: Siege of Buda (1603)
commanders: Habsburg forces vs. Ottoman garrison
importance: A failed attempt by Habsburg forces to reclaim the administrative heart of Ottoman Hungary.

name: Naval Battle of Preveza
commanders: Hayreddin Barbarossa; Andrea Doria
importance: Consolidated Ottoman naval dominance in the Mediterranean for decades.
casualties: Heavy losses for the Holy League fleet.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Sudak
commanders: Gedik Ahmed Pasha
importance: Consolidation of Ottoman control over the Crimean coast.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Balaklava
commanders: Gedik Ahmed Pasha
importance: Further reduced Genoese coastal strongholds.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Kerch
commanders: Gedik Ahmed Pasha
importance: Secured the strategic entrance to the Sea of Azov.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Azov (Tana)
commanders: Gedik Ahmed Pasha
importance: Established Ottoman dominance over the northern Black Sea and the Don River trade route.

name: Battle of Giurgiu
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Wallachia & Habsburg allies
importance: Part of the Long Turkish War, checking Ottoman expansion in the Danube region.

name: Battle of Cecora
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Poland-Lithuania
importance: Major engagement during the Polish-Ottoman War, ending in the death of Hetman Stanisław Żółkiewski.

name: Battle of Zhovti Vody
commanders: Cossacks & Crimean Khanate; Poland-Lithuania
importance: First major victory of Khmelnytsky's Uprising.

name: Capture of Azov
commanders: Don Cossacks; Ottoman Empire
importance: Temporarily severed the Ottoman hold on the Don-Volga trade route.

name: Siege of Azov
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Don Cossacks
importance: Failed Ottoman attempt to regain Azov.

name: Ottoman Recovery of Azov
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Don Cossacks
importance: Cossacks withdrew, returning the fortress to Ottoman control.

name: Ottoman–Polish Border Campaigns
commanders: Ottoman & Crimean forces; Poland-Lithuania
importance: Series of raids destabilizing the Dniester border region.

name: Destruction of the Great Horde
commanders: Crimean Khanate; Great Horde
importance: Ended the remnants of the Golden Horde, clearing the way for Crimean hegemony.

name: Capture of Arta
commanders: Ottoman forces; Local rulers
importance: The capture of Arta expanded Ottoman administrative control across Epirus.

name: Siege of the Hexamilion Wall
commanders: Murad II; Constantine Palaiologos
importance: Ottoman forces breached the defensive wall at the Isthmus of Corinth, opening the Peloponnese to invasion.

name: Siege of Astrakhan
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Tsardom of Russia
importance: Failed Ottoman attempt to capture Astrakhan and control the Volga trade route.

name: Conquest of Thessaly completed
commanders: Ottoman Rumelian forces; Thessalian local powers
importance: Extended direct Ottoman authority into central Greece.

name: Capture of Vidin
commanders: Ottoman Danube forces; Bulgarian defenders
importance: Ended the last major Bulgarian political center.

name: Expansion into Albania
commanders: Ottoman frontier forces; Albanian lords
importance: Laid groundwork for the later Albanian campaigns.

name: Battle of Ankara
commanders: Bayezid I; Timur
importance: Outside the Europe-only frame but essential to the pause in European expansion.

name: End of Ottoman Interregnum
commanders: Mehmed I
importance: Restored dynastic unity after the civil war.

name: Capture of Valona (Vlora)
commanders: Ottoman forces; Albanian/Venetian local authorities
importance: Improved Ottoman access to the Adriatic coast.

name: First Siege of Constantinople
commanders: Murad II; Byzantine defenders
importance: Early failed Ottoman attempt against the Byzantine capital.

name: Capture of Thessaloniki
commanders: Murad II; Venetian defenders
importance: Secured the major Macedonian port for the Ottomans.

name: Albanian campaigns
commanders: Ottoman Rumelian forces; Albanian rebels and lords
importance: Part of the long contest for Albania before Skanderbeg's revolt.

name: Capture of Smederevo
commanders: Murad II; Serbian Despotate defenders
importance: Temporarily eliminated Serbia as an independent barrier.

name: Siege of Belgrade
commanders: Ottoman forces; Hungarian defenders
importance: Showed Belgrade's continued strength as Hungary's southern gate.

name: Battle of Niš (Long Campaign)
commanders: Janos Hunyadi and Wladyslaw III vs. Kasim Pasha / Ottoman commanders
importance: Major Christian victory during the Long Campaign, opening the Balkan offensive before Varna.

name: Battle of Râmnic
commanders: Stephen III of Moldavia vs. Basarab IV and Ottoman forces
importance: Moldavian invasion of Wallachia resulting in the rout of Wallachian-Ottoman forces following the death of Mehmed II.
casualties: Entire Wallachian army annihilated; significant Moldavian losses.

name: Battle of Chițcani
commanders: Stefan Kunicki & Ștefan Petriceicu vs. Yala-Pasha & Ali, bey of Tighina
importance: Cossack and Moldavian allied victory during Kunicki's campaign at the opening of the Polish-Ottoman War (1683–1699).

name: Battle of Reni
commanders: Stefan Kunicki, Andriy Mohyla & Ștefan Petriceicu vs. Haci II Giray & Ottoman forces
importance: Major engagement during the Great Turkish War that effectively ended Kunicki's campaign following initial Christian successes.

name: Battle of Varna
commanders: Murad II; Wladyslaw III and Janos Hunyadi
importance: Destroyed the crusade of Varna.
casualties: King Wladyslaw killed; heavy Christian losses.

name: Battle of Obreška
commanders: Croatian Ban Petar Erdody vs. Bosnian Sanjakbey Mustafa Pasha Sokolović
importance: Successfully checked the Ottoman advance following the fall of Krupa, leading to the ennoblement of Petar Erdody as a count.

name: Battle of Gorjani
commanders: Habsburg Monarchy (Johann Katzianer) vs. Ottoman Empire (Governor of Belgrade forces)
importance: A decisive defeat for the Habsburgs that saw the annihilation of their 24,000-man army, halting imperial offensive ambitions in the region following the broken Treaty of Konstantiniyye.

name: Siege of Buda
commanders: Suleiman the Magnificent vs. Ferdinand I
importance: Suleiman successfully captured Buda after intensive artillery bombardment, restoring and installing John Zápolya as an Ottoman vassal king over Hungary before marching on Vienna.

name: Battle of Srebrenica (1411)
commanders: Kingdom of Bosnia (Tvrtko II, Hrvoje Vukčić) vs. Hungary (Sigismund of Luxembourg, Stefan Lazarević)
importance: Sigismund of Luxembourg seized the city, granting it to Serbian Despot Stefan Lazarević, establishing long-term Hungarian influence over the silver mines.

name: Battle of Srebrenica (1444)
commanders: Kingdom of Bosnia (Stjepan Tomaš) vs. Ottoman Empire / Serbian Despotate
importance: King Stjepan Tomaš successfully reconquered the city, ending a long period of Hungarian-Despotate administration.

name: Battle of Srebrenica (1445)
commanders: Kingdom of Bosnia (Ivaniš Pavlović) vs. Serbian Despotate (Đurađ Branković)
importance: The Bosnian forces pushed back the Despotate of Serbia to maintain control over the Podrinje mining region.

name: Battle of Srebrenica (1449)
commanders: Kingdom of Bosnia (Stjepan Tomaš) vs. Serbian Despotate
importance: A final re-conquest by Stjepan Tomaš against the Despotate, cementing control shortly before the intensifying Ottoman offensive in the region.

name: Battle of Bileća
commanders: Kingdom of Bosnia (Vlatko Vuković) vs. Ottoman Empire (Lala Shahin Pasha)
importance: A significant early defensive success for the Bosnian Kingdom, halting an Ottoman plundering raid into the Hum region.

name: Siege of Ključ
commanders: Ottoman Empire (Mahmud Pasha Angelović) vs. Kingdom of Bosnia (Stephen Tomašević)
importance: Led to the capture and execution of the last Bosnian King, Stephen Tomašević, and the rapid collapse of Bosnian resistance across 70+ towns.
casualties: Heavy (Bosnian forces fled or were captured)

name: Battle of Una
commanders: Kingdom of Croatia (Matthias Geréb, Vuk Grgurević) vs. Ottoman Sanjak of Bosnia
importance: One of the first major Croatian victories against the Ottoman Empire; it successfully checked Ottoman incursions and led to a 7-year truce.

name: Battle of Vrpile
commanders: Kingdom of Croatia (Ladislav of Egervár, Bernardin Frankopan) vs. Ottoman raiding force
importance: A successful ambush of an Ottoman raiding party returning from Carniola; it demonstrated effective frontier defense tactics.

name: Battle of Novigrad
commanders: Kingdom of Croatia (Petar Berislavić) vs. Ottoman Bosnia Eyalet forces
importance: A heavy defeat for the Croatian forces led by Ban Petar Berislavić, illustrating the increasing military pressure on the Adriatic coastal defenses.

name: Battle of Hrastovica
commanders: Kingdom of Croatia (Local castellan) vs. Ottoman Empire (Malkoč-beg)
importance: A tactical defensive success for the newly formed Hrastovica captaincy, demonstrating the effectiveness of localized garrison fortifications in halting Ottoman incursions into the Banija region.

name: Relief of Jajce
commanders: Kingdom of Croatia (Petar Berislavić) vs. Ottoman Empire (Gazi Husrev-beg)
importance: Although the attempt to capture nearby Ottoman forts failed, the relief expedition successfully reprovisioned the Jajce garrison, extending the lifespan of this critical Christian defensive salient by several years.

name: Siege of Knin
commanders: Ottoman Empire (Ghazi Husrev-beg) vs. Kingdom of Croatia (Mihajlo Vojković)
importance: The loss of Knin, the royal capital of the Kingdom of Croatia, was a devastating blow that forced the redistribution of Ottoman forces and established a permanent Ottoman administrative seat in the region.

name: Battle of Belaj
commanders: Habsburg/Croatian forces (Ivan Karlović, Bernardin Ričan) vs. Ottoman Empire (Gazi Husrev-beg)
importance: A significant defensive success that routed an Ottoman raiding force returning from Carniola, though marred by the friendly-fire incident that nearly killed the Croatian Ban.

name: Battle of Stephaniana
commanders: Serbian Empire (Preljub) vs. Emirate of Aydin (Umur Beg)
importance: The first major military engagement between Serbian and Turkish forces, though it did not stop Dušan's expansion into Macedonia.

name: Siege of Mirandola
commanders: Piero Strozzi vs. Papal-Imperial commanders
importance: The defenders successfully resisted the Papal-Imperial siege, preserving Parma's French-backed position.

name: Treaty of Chambord
commanders: Henry II of France; Maurice of Saxony and German Protestant princes
importance: France allied with the German Protestant princes against Charles V, paving the way for French expansion into Lorraine.

name: Truce ending the War of Parma
commanders: Charles V; Henry II; Ottavio Farnese
importance: Ended active fighting in the War of Parma while leaving broader Franco-Habsburg tensions unresolved.

name: Second Schmalkaldic War (Princes' Revolt)
commanders: Maurice of Saxony, Henry II of France vs. Charles V
importance: Forced Charles V to accept the Peace of Passau while France secured Metz, Toul, and Verdun.

name: Siege of Metz
commanders: Francis, Duke of Guise vs. Charles V
importance: France successfully defended Metz, frustrating Charles V's attempt to recover the Three Bishoprics.
casualties: Heavy Imperial losses from combat and disease.

name: Siege of Thérouanne
commanders: Emmanuel Philibert, Imperial commanders vs. French garrison
importance: Thérouanne was captured and deliberately destroyed on Charles V's orders.

name: Battle of Demotika
commanders: Serbian/Bulgarian forces (Gradislav Borilović) vs. Ottoman Beylik (Süleyman Pasha)
importance: A landmark engagement marking the first major victory of Ottoman troops on European soil, leading to the occupation of Gallipoli.

name: Battle of Sırpsındığı
commanders: Serbian/Bulgarian/Wallachian forces (Mrnjavčević brothers) vs. Ottoman Empire (Hacı İlbey)
importance: The 'Rout of the Serbs'; a major Ottoman success that solidified their presence near Adrianople (Edirne).

name: Battle of Samokov
commanders: Serbian/Bulgarian forces (Uglješa Mrnjavčević, Ivan Shishman) vs. Ottoman Empire (Lala Shahin Pasha)
importance: The swift Ottoman victory left the Serbian and Bulgarian forces disorganized and fleeing, opening the path for further Ottoman penetration.

name: Battle of Hațeg
commanders: Kingdom of Hungary (Miklós Csáki) vs. Ottoman Empire
importance: Marked the beginning of the War of the South Danube (1420–1432), where Ottoman forces devastated the Transylvanian frontier.

name: Battle of Szőlős
commanders: Jovan Nenad vs. Péter Perényi
importance: A significant engagement where the forces of the 'Black Man' Jovan Nenad defeated the Hungarian nobility, establishing a short-lived autonomous Serbian entity.

name: Battle of Sződfalva
commanders: Jovan Nenad vs. Péter Perényi and Imre Czibak
importance: The decisive defeat of Jovan Nenad's army, leading to the collapse of his autonomous principality and his death.

name: Battle of Tarcal
commanders: John Zápolya vs. Archduke Ferdinand of Austria
importance: Ferdinand's success at Tarcal solidified Habsburg claims to the Hungarian throne and forced Zápolya into a defensive posture.

name: Battle of Szina
commanders: John Zápolya vs. Bálint Török and Johann Katzianer
importance: A major blow to John Zápolya, pushing him to seek Ottoman military assistance against Ferdinand.

name: Battle of Feldioara
commanders: Petru Rareș (Moldavia) vs. Bálint Török and István Majláth
importance: Demonstrated the reach of Moldavian influence under Petru Rareș, who briefly exerted control over Transylvanian regions after the defeat of Habsburg forces.

name: Second Battle of Kosovo
commanders: Murad II; Janos Hunyadi
importance: Confirmed Ottoman dominance in the Balkans.

name: Fall of Constantinople
commanders: Mehmed II; Constantine XI
importance: Ended the Byzantine Empire and created the Ottoman imperial capital.

name: First Siege of Novo Brdo
commanders: Mehmed II's forces; Serbian defenders
importance: Captured one of the Balkans' richest mining centers.

name: Siege of Belgrade
commanders: Mehmed II; Janos Hunyadi
importance: Delayed Ottoman advance into Hungary for decades.

name: Capture of Athens
commanders: Mehmed II; Duchy of Athens
importance: Brought Athens into the Ottoman sphere.

name: Capture of Smederevo
commanders: Mehmed II; Serbian defenders
importance: Ended the Serbian Despotate as an independent state.

name: Conquest of the Morea
commanders: Mehmed II; Palaiologos despots
importance: Ended Byzantine successor rule in the Peloponnese.

name: Conquest of Trebizond
commanders: Mehmed II; David Komnenos
importance: Outside the Europe-only frame but included as the final Byzantine successor conquest.

name: Wallachian campaign
commanders: Mehmed II; Vlad III
importance: Reasserted Ottoman pressure over Wallachia after Vlad's raids.

name: Conquest of Bosnia
commanders: Mehmed II; Stephen Tomasevic
importance: Created the foundation for Ottoman Bosnia.

name: First Siege of Kruje
commanders: Mehmed II; Skanderbeg and Albanian defenders
importance: Major failed Ottoman attempt to break Albanian resistance.

name: Second Siege of Kruje
commanders: Mehmed II; Albanian defenders
importance: Albanian resistance continued despite heavy pressure.

name: Capture of Caffa
commanders: Gedik Ahmed Pasha; Genoese defenders
importance: Brought the Genoese Black Sea colonies under Ottoman control.

name: Third Siege of Kruje
commanders: Ottoman forces; Venetian-Albanian defenders
importance: Broke the most famous Albanian fortress resistance after Skanderbeg's death.

name: Siege of Shkoder begins
commanders: Mehmed II's forces; Venetian defenders
importance: Opened the final phase of Ottoman conquest in northern Albania.

name: Capture of Shkoder
commanders: Ottoman forces; Venetian defenders
importance: Confirmed Ottoman control after Venice ceded the fortress.

name: Siege of Otranto
commanders: Gedik Ahmed Pasha; Neapolitan defenders
importance: Demonstrated Ottoman ability to project power into Italy.

name: Capture of Kilia
commanders: Bayezid II; Moldavian defenders
importance: Cut Moldavia away from a key Danube-Black Sea outlet.

name: Capture of Akkerman
commanders: Bayezid II; Moldavian defenders
importance: Completed Ottoman seizure of Moldavia's Black Sea access.

name: Battle of Zonchio
commanders: Kemal Reis; Venetian fleet
importance: One of the first major naval battles using shipboard artillery decisively.

name: Battle of Karpathos
commanders: Kemal Reis vs. Nicolas Centurione
importance: Kemal Reis defeated the Knights Hospitaller fleet between Karpathos and Crete, capturing five ships and the enemy commander
casualties: 1 Hospitaller ship sunk, 5 captured; light Ottoman losses

name: Battle of Adana (1486)
commanders: Hersekzade Ahmed Pasha vs. Mamluk Sultanate
importance: Combined Ottoman-Janissary forces were defeated before Adana, forcing Karagöz Mehmed to flee and Hersekzade Ahmed into captivity, restoring Cilicia to Mamluk control
casualties: Heavy Ottoman losses and capture of Hersekzade Ahmed Pasha

name: Battle of Ağaçarıyı
commanders: Hadim Ali Pasha vs. Mamluk Sultanate
importance: Major open-field clash near Adana where the Ottoman right flank collapsed and Karaman soldiers fled, forcing a full Ottoman retreat
casualties: Heavy Ottoman casualties; field conceded to Mamluks

name: Siege of Adana (1488–1489)
commanders: Hadim Ali Pasha vs. Mamluk Sultanate
importance: Mamluks successfully besieged and captured Adana following the Ottoman defeat at Ağaçarıyı, cementing Mamluk control over Cilicia

name: Mamluk Offensive against Kayseri
commanders: Mamluk Sultanate vs. Hersekzade Ahmed Pasha
importance: Mamluks advanced into Karaman and laid siege to Kayseri before retreating upon the approach of Hersekzade Ahmed Pasha's relief army, leading to the 1491 peace treaty

name: Defeat in Bukovina
commanders: John I Albert vs. Moldavian and Ottoman forces
importance: Subsequent rout of retreating Polish forces in Bukovina shortly after the Cosmin Forest disaster, resulting in thousands more killed

name: Battle of Modon
commanders: Kemal Reis vs. Venetian Fleet
importance: Ottoman fleet defeated Venice again, allowing Kemal Reis to bombard and capture the vital fortress town of Modon
casualties: Heavy Venetian losses; fall of Modon and Coron ('two eyes of the Republic')

name: Siege and Capture of Cephalonia
commanders: Gonzalo de Córdoba vs. Ottoman Garrison
importance: A joint Spanish-Venetian force captured Cephalonia, temporarily halting the Ottoman offensive on Venetian eastern territories

name: Capture of Durazzo
commanders: Feriz Beg vs. Republic of Venice
importance: Feriz Beg captured the strategic stronghold of Durazzo in Venetian Albania

name: Capture of Coron
commanders: Ottoman forces; Venetian defenders
importance: Consolidated Ottoman gains in the southwestern Peloponnese.

name: Siege of Belgrade
commanders: Suleiman I; Hungarian defenders
importance: Opened the Danube road into Hungary.

name: Siege of Rhodes
commanders: Suleiman I; Philippe Villiers de L'Isle-Adam
importance: Ended Hospitaller rule on Rhodes.

name: Battle of Mohacs
commanders: Suleiman I; Louis II
importance: Collapsed the medieval Kingdom of Hungary.
casualties: King Louis II killed; heavy Hungarian losses.

name: First Siege of Vienna
commanders: Suleiman I; Wilhelm von Roggendorf
importance: Checked Ottoman advance into Austria.
casualties: Attrition from weather and siege fighting.

name: Siege of Koszeg
commanders: Suleiman I; Nikola Jurisic
importance: Delayed Suleiman's march and protected Vienna.
casualties: Heavy siege losses not securely recorded.

name: Capture of Klis
commanders: Ottoman Bosnian forces; Croatian defenders
importance: Strengthened the Ottoman-Venetian-Habsburg frontier in Dalmatia.

name: Capture of Buda
commanders: Suleiman I; Habsburg and Hungarian factions
importance: Created Budin Eyalet and Ottoman Hungary.
casualties: Political collapse more decisive than battlefield loss.

name: Capture of Esztergom
commanders: Suleiman I; Habsburg defenders
importance: Secured a major Danube fortress north of Buda.

name: Capture of Szekesfehervar
commanders: Suleiman I; Habsburg defenders
importance: Captured the traditional coronation city of the Hungarian kings.

name: Capture of Visegrad
commanders: Ottoman Danube forces; Habsburg defenders
importance: Strengthened Ottoman control along the Danube bend.

name: Campaign in Transylvania
commanders: Ottoman commanders and Transylvanian factions; Habsburg forces
importance: Reinforced Transylvania's role as a contested vassal-buffer state.

name: Battle of Brest
commanders: Ivan Drašković vs. Achmed Hafis Pasha
importance: A key defensive victory that successfully halted the advance of the Ottoman force led by the Beylerbey of Vidin into Croatian territory.

name: Battle of Brest
commanders: Hasan Pasha Predojević vs. Tamás Erdődy & Kristofor Peuchel
importance: Fought near Brest in the Kingdom of Croatia during the Ottoman-Habsburg wars; Ottoman forces under Bosnian beglerbeg Hasan Pasha Predojević crushed combined Croatian and Styrian forces led by Ban Tamás Erdődy, leading to the capture of Brest and setting the stage for the subsequent siege of Sisak
casualties: 800+ allied casualties; heavy defeat and rout of Croatian and Styrian forces

name: Siege of Temesvar
commanders: Kara Ahmed Pasha; Istvan Losonczy
importance: Created Temesvar Eyalet.

name: Siege of Eger
commanders: Kara Ahmed Pasha; Istvan Dobo
importance: Famous Habsburg-Hungarian defensive success in northern Hungary.

name: Great Siege of Malta
commanders: Serdar Lala Mustafa Pasha (Ottoman, ~25,000 men) vs. Knights Hospitaller & Don Garcia's Spanish relief force
importance: Saved Malta and the Knights Hospitaller, a key Spanish ally protecting southern Italy; Spanish relief force of 8,000 forced Ottoman evacuation
casualties: Heavy losses on Ottoman side (not quantified in source)

name: Battle of Călugăreni
commanders: Michael the Brave vs. Sinan Pasha
result: Tactical Wallachian victory, strategic Ottoman advance
importance: A major defensive stand by Wallachian forces against the Ottoman campaign aimed at occupying Bucharest and Târgoviște.

name: Battle of Leobersdorf
commanders: Sebastian Schertlin von Burtenbach, Johann Katzianer vs. Kazim Bey
importance: Habsburg forces trapped and destroyed Kazim Bey's Ottoman light cavalry raiding party after they were forced into a narrow valley, securing the southern approach to Vienna.

name: Siege of Drégelypalánk
commanders: György Szondi vs. Ottoman Empire
importance: A legendary symbol of heroism; Szondi and his small garrison fought to the death against overwhelming odds.

name: Siege of Szolnok
commanders: Ottoman Empire (Pasha Ahmed Ali) vs. Lőrinc Nyáry
importance: The rapid collapse of the fortress due to mercenary desertion caused widespread panic in the region, directly impacting the morale of the defenders at the upcoming Siege of Eger.

name: Siege of Eger
commanders: Ottoman Empire (Mehmed III) vs. Habsburg garrison
importance: The fall of Eger provided the Ottomans with a critical strategic stronghold in Upper Hungary, following the surrender of the demoralized garrison.

name: Battle of Palást
commanders: Erasmus von Teufel vs. Arslan Bey
importance: The Ottoman victory, catalyzed by a gunpowder explosion in the Habsburg camp, shattered Christian resistance in the region and forced the abandonment of Central Slovakia.

name: Capture of Nógrád
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg garrison
importance: Consolidated Ottoman control over the northern territories of the Eyalet of Buda.

name: Battle of Khotyn
commanders: Jan Karol Chodkiewicz vs. Sultan Osman II
importance: The combined Polish-Lithuanian and Cossack army successfully halted the Ottoman advance near the Dniester River.

name: Battle of Martynów
commanders: Stanisław Koniecpolski vs. Crimean Tatars
importance: Renowned for tactical innovation, effectively neutralizing a massive Tatar mobile force.

name: Battle of Krbava Field
commanders: Ottoman Empire (Bayezid II) vs. Kingdom of Croatia
importance: A catastrophic defeat for the Croatian nobility that accelerated the collapse of central military resistance against Ottoman expansion.

name: Siege of Buda (1530)
commanders: Habsburg (Ferdinand I) vs. John Zápolya
importance: Unsuccessful Habsburg attempt to reclaim Buda, highlighting the deep division of the Hungarian throne.

name: Siege of Novi Zrin
commanders: Ottoman (Köprülü Fazıl Ahmed Pasha) vs. Croatian forces (Nikola Zrinski)
importance: The destruction of the border fortress of Novi Zrin removed a key defensive bastion for northern Croatia.

name: Battle of Nagyszőllős
commanders: George II Rákóczi vs. Crimean Tatars
importance: A decisive defeat for Rákóczi's forces that ended his ambitions for the Polish throne and severely weakened Transylvanian influence.
casualties: High; Rákóczi's army was largely destroyed or captured.

name: Siege of Szigetvar
commanders: Suleiman I; Nikola Subic Zrinski
importance: Suleiman died during the campaign.

name: Peace of Adrianople
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Habsburg Monarchy
importance: Confirmed the central Hungarian settlement after Suleiman's wars.

name: Invasion of Cyprus
commanders: Lala Mustafa Pasha; Venetian Cyprus
importance: Opened the Ottoman-Venetian war over Cyprus.
casualties: Heavy siege casualties during the campaign.

name: Capture of Famagusta
commanders: Lala Mustafa Pasha; Marcantonio Bragadin
importance: Completed Ottoman conquest of Cyprus.

name: Battle of Lepanto
commanders: Muezzinzade Ali Pasha; Don John of Austria
importance: Major Holy League victory over the Ottoman fleet.

name: Battle of Molodi
commanders: Devlet I Giray and Ottoman-supported Crimean forces; Mikhail Vorotynsky and Dmitry Khvorostinin
importance: Checked Crimean-Ottoman pressure on Muscovy after the 1571 burning of Moscow; included as a northern frontier reference outside the core Ottoman Europe frame.
casualties: Heavy Crimean-Tatar losses reported; exact totals vary by source.

name: Battle of Sisak
commanders: Hasan Pasha Predojevic; Habsburg-Croatian forces
importance: Sparked the Long Turkish War.
casualties: Ottoman commander killed; heavy Ottoman losses.

name: Siege of Shkodra
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Venice and League of Lezhë
importance: A landmark siege of the Rozafa Castle that effectively ended Venetian influence in Albania and secured Ottoman dominance in the region.

name: Siege of Kraków (1657)
commanders: Jerzy Lubomirski & Melchior von Hatzfeldt vs. Paul Wirtz & János Bethlen
importance: Combined Polish and Holy Roman Empire forces besieged and successfully recaptured Kraków after a two-year Swedish-Transylvanian occupation
casualties: Garrison capitulation following the destruction of Rákóczi's army at Czarny Ostrow

name: Conquest of Chios
commanders: Piyale Pasha vs. Genoese rulers of Chios
importance: Removed a Genoese (Spanish-allied) possession in the Aegean

name: Strike on the Pula Coast (1566)
commanders: Ottoman fleet vs. Kingdom of Naples
importance: Continued pressure on Spanish-allied Italian coasts following the Chios conquest

name: Kılıç Ali Pasha's Attempted Fleet to Almería
commanders: Kılıç Ali Pasha
importance: Attempted to bring soldiers, provisions and weapons to aid the Morisco rebels of Granada

name: Ottoman Aid Landed near Almería
commanders: Kılıç Ali Pasha
importance: Managed to deliver 400-500 soldiers and provisions/weapons to the Morisco rebels

name: Battle of Mezokeresztes
commanders: Mehmed III; Habsburg-Transylvanian army
importance: Followed the fall of Eger and helped shape Egri Eyalet.

name: Uprising in Banat
commanders: Bishop Teodor of Vršac & Sava Temišvarac vs. Ottoman Empire forces
importance: A rebellion by local Serbs numbering around 5,000 during the initial stage of the Long Turkish War in the Eyalet of Temeşvar; rebels successfully captured several towns before being crushed by the Ottoman army, leading to severe reprisals including the burning of Saint Sava's relics

name: Siege of Nagykanizsa
commanders: Tiryaki Hasan Pasha; Ferdinand's forces
importance: Secured Kanije Eyalet against Habsburg counterattack.

name: Peace of Zsitvatorok
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Habsburg Monarchy
importance: Ended the Long Turkish War and altered Ottoman-Habsburg diplomatic relations.

name: Capture of Oradea
commanders: Kose Ali Pasha; Transylvanian-Habsburg defenders
importance: Created Varat Eyalet.

name: Capture of Nove Zamky (Ersekujvar)
commanders: Koprulu Fazil Ahmed Pasha; Adam Forgach
importance: Created Uyvar Eyalet in Upper Hungary.

name: Battle of Saint Gotthard
commanders: Koprulu Fazil Ahmed Pasha; Raimondo Montecuccoli
importance: Checked Ottoman advance after Uyvar.

name: Fall of Candia
commanders: Koprulu Fazil Ahmed Pasha; Venetian commanders
importance: Completed Ottoman conquest of Crete after a long siege.

name: Siege of Kamianets-Podilskyi
commanders: Mehmed IV and Koprulu Fazil Ahmed Pasha; Polish defenders
importance: Led to the creation of Podolia Eyalet.

name: Siege of Lviv
commanders: Ottoman-Cossack-Tatar forces; Commonwealth defenders
importance: Part of the Ottoman-Commonwealth war following Kamianets.

name: Battle of Khotyn
commanders: Jan Sobieski; Hussein Pasha
importance: Restored Commonwealth prestige after Buchach.

name: Treaty of Zurawno
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
importance: Confirmed Ottoman possession of Podolia in the short term.

name: Treaty of Constantinople (1494)
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Venice
importance: Established early stable relations and commercial arrangements.

name: Treaty of Constantinople (1533)
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Habsburg Monarchy
importance: Long-lasting peace and mutual recognition of borders.

name: Treaty of Adrianople (1547)
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Ferdinand I
importance: Ferdinand I recognized Ottoman control over most of Hungary.

name: Peace of Amasya
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Safavid Iran
importance: First official peace between Ottomans and Safavids.

name: Treaty of Constantinople (1590)
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Safavid Iran
importance: Ottomans secured vast areas of the Caucasus.

name: Siege of Veszprém
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg
importance: The first engagement of the Long Turkish War, marking the resumption of large-scale hostilities.

name: Siege of Várpalota
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg
importance: Followed the fall of Veszprém, forcing the Habsburgs onto the defensive in western Hungary.

name: Siege of Győr
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg
importance: A major strategic loss for the Habsburgs; Győr was a key fortress protecting the road to Vienna.

name: Siege of Komárom
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg
importance: Part of the rapid 1594 Ottoman push to seize critical Danube crossings.

name: Siege of Esztergom
commanders: Habsburg (Mansfeld) vs. Ottoman Empire
importance: A major tactical success that reclaimed the strategic fortress city of Esztergom from Ottoman control.

name: Siege of Visegrád
commanders: Habsburg (Mansfeld) vs. Ottoman Empire
importance: The capture of Visegrád further solidified the Habsburg hold on the Danube line and the route towards Buda.

name: Battle of Șelimbăr
commanders: Michael the Brave vs. Andrew Báthory
importance: Michael the Brave defeated the Transylvanian prince, allowing him to occupy Alba Iulia and begin his brief unification of the Romanian principalities.

name: Siege of Castelnuovo
commanders: Francisco de Sarmiento vs. Hayreddin Barbarossa & Ulamen
importance: An Ottoman army of over 50,000 men besieged and captured Castelnuovo after a brutal defense by a Spanish tercio, ending Christian attempts to control the Eastern Mediterranean
casualties: Heavy Ottoman losses (~8,000 killed); almost all 3,500+ Spanish defenders killed or captured

name: Siege of Navarino (1572)
commanders: John of Austria, Álvaro de Bazán & Alexander Farnese vs. Occhiali
importance: A Holy League armada led by John of Austria failed to capture the Ottoman-held castle at Navarino and withdrew following heavy resistance and reports of large reinforcements
casualties: 750 allied troops killed; 1 Ottoman ship lost

name: Battle of Mirăslău
commanders: Michael the Brave vs. Giorgio Basta
importance: A decisive defeat for Michael the Brave that ended his rule in Transylvania and forced his temporary retreat.

name: Siege of Nagyvárad (1660)
commanders: Máté Balogh, János Rácz & Mihály Ibrányi vs. Ali Pasha & Szejdi Ahmed Pasha
importance: A 50,000-strong Ottoman army besieged and captured the strategic fortress of Várad (Oradea) after a 44-day siege, leading to the establishment of the Eyalet of Várad and the loss of Transylvanian independence
casualties: Heavy losses; garrison reduced from 850 to 300 men before surrender

name: Battle of Nagyvárad
commanders: László Rákóczy & Zsigmond Pethő vs. Kucuk Pasha (Ottoman Garrison)
importance: Fought during the Austro-Turkish War; a joint Hungarian-German force led by László Rákóczy launched a surprise attack and entered Ottoman-held Nagyvárad, but was ultimately ousted after looting the town, resulting in heavy losses and the death of Rákóczy
casualties: Heavy losses on both sides, including the death of Hungarian commander László Rákóczy

name: Siege of Pskov
commanders: Stephen Báthory & Jan Zamojski vs. Vasili Skopin-Shuisky & Ivan Shuisky
result: Disputed — tactical Russian defensive success (siege repelled) but strategic Polish-Lithuanian victory via the Treaty of Jam Zapolski
importance: Final major action of the Livonian War; a 31,000-strong Polish-Lithuanian-Hungarian-Bohemian-Wallachian-German army failed to take the city despite repeated assaults, mining attempts, and a five-month blockade, while Russian defenders (~4,000 troops and ~12,000 armed citizens) conducted 46 sallies; ended with the Treaty of Jam Zapolski, in which Russia renounced claims to Livonia and Polotsk in exchange for the return of captured territories

name: Treaty of Nasuh Pasha
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Safavid Iran
importance: First time Ottomans agreed to cede conquered territory.

name: Treaty of Busza
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
importance: Addressed Moldavian affairs and Cossack–Tatar raids.

name: Treaty of Serav
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Safavid Iran
importance: Reduced the annual silk tribute requirement.

name: Treaty of Khotyn
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
importance: Ended the war; borders remained largely unchanged.

name: Treaty of Zuhab
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Safavid Iran
importance: Defined the modern border between Iraq and Iran.

name: Peace of Vasvár
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Habsburg Monarchy
importance: Despite Habsburg victory at St. Gotthard, Ottomans kept key gains.

name: Treaty of Buchach
commanders: Ottoman Empire; Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
importance: Poland agreed to tribute and loss of Podolia (later rejected).

name: Siege of Vienna
commanders: Kara Mustafa Pasha; Ernst Rudiger von Starhemberg and Jan III Sobieski
importance: Turning point of the Great Turkish War and the end of Ottoman expansion in central Europe.
casualties: Heavy Ottoman losses and abandoned camp.

name: Battle of Molodi
commanders: Devlet I Giray and Ottoman-supported Crimean forces; Mikhail Vorotynsky and Dmitry Khvorostinin
importance: Checked Crimean-Ottoman pressure on Muscovy after the 1571 burning of Moscow; included as a northern frontier reference.
casualties: Heavy Crimean-Tatar losses reported; exact totals vary by source.

name: Battle of Molodi
commanders: Crimean-Ottoman vs Russia
importance: Checked northern expansion.

name: Battle of Molodi
commanders: Crimean-Ottoman vs Russia
importance: Checked northern expansion.

name: Attack on Chilia (Kilia)
commanders: Ottoman naval/land forces; Moldavian defenders under Alexandru cel Bun
importance: First recorded Ottoman military attempt to capture a stronghold in Moldavia.

name: Battle of Vaslui (Podul Înalt)
commanders: Hadım Suleiman Pasha; Stephen the Great (Ștefan cel Mare)
importance: One of the greatest Christian tactical victories against Ottoman forces in the 15th century.

name: Battle of Valea Albă (Războieni)
commanders: Mehmed II; Stephen the Great
importance: Mehmed II defeated the main Moldavian field army but failed to permanently subdue the principality.

name: Siege of Neamț Fortress
commanders: Mehmed II; Moldavian garrison defenders
importance: The fortress held out successfully, forcing Mehmed II to withdraw due to supply shortages and plague.

name: Battle of Komarno
commanders: John III Sobieski & Stefan Bidzinski vs. Nurredin-Sultan & Petro Doroshenko
importance: A premier engagement of Jan III Sobieski's autumn expedition during the Polish-Ottoman War; Crown Hetman Sobieski led a grueling 57-kilometer march in heavy rain to surprise a superior Tatar-Cossack force near Komarno, routing them into the Wereszyca river and liberating approximately 20,000 captive civilians
casualties: 9,300 Crimean Tatars and allies killed or captured; minimal Polish-Lithuanian losses

name: Battle of Trembowla
commanders: Jan Samuel Chrzanowski & Anna Dorota Chrzanowska vs. Ibrahim Shyshman
importance: A legendary defense during the Polish-Ottoman War (1672–1676); a tiny garrison of around 80 soldiers and local volunteers under Captain Chrzanowski and his resolute wife Anna Dorota successfully held the small Trembowla castle against a massive Ottoman-Tatar army for over three weeks until the approach of Jan III Sobieski's forces forced the Turks to lift the siege
casualties: Heavy garrison and defender losses; significant casualties inflicted on the besieging Ottoman-Tatar forces

name: Suleiman's Moldavian Campaign (Capture of Suceava)
commanders: Suleiman the Magnificent; Petru Rareș (deposed)
importance: Suleiman captured the capital, annexed southern Bessarabia (Tighina/Bender), and firmly asserted vassal tracking over foreign policy.
casualties: Minimal battlefield combat losses; highly strategic campaign.

name: Siege of Suceava (1497)
commanders: John I Albert vs. Stephen III
importance: Unsuccessful four-week Polish siege of Suceava that forced King John I Albert to begin retreating from Moldavia
casualties: Heavy Polish losses from resistance and disease

name: Moldavian Campaign of Bohdan Khmelnytsky
commanders: Bohdan Khmelnytsky & İslâm III Giray vs. Vasile Lupu
importance: Joint invasion of Moldavia that forced Vasile Lupu to pay heavy tribute, break his Polish alliance, and agree to the marriage of his daughter Ruxandra to Tymofiy Khmelnytsky
casualties: Heavy Moldavian losses and widespread looting/enslavement

name: Moldavian Campaign (Battle of Roșcani)
commanders: Ottoman-Wallachian coalition forces; John III the Terrible (Ioan Vodă cel Cumplit)
importance: Suppressed a major anti-Ottoman rebellion and reasserted sovereign provincial tribute authority.
casualties: Heavy Moldavian rebel forces wiped out.

name: Battle of Savra
commanders: Hayreddin Pasha; Balša II of Zeta
importance: First major Ottoman military victory in Albania; established baseline suzerainty over regional princes.

name: Occupation of Krujë
commanders: Ottoman Rumelian forces; Thopia family defenders
importance: Brought a highly critical northern Albanian fortress under direct garrison control.

name: Conquest of Vlorë, Berat and Kanina
commanders: Evrenosoglu Ali Bey; Rugina Balšić
importance: Secured southern Albania and established a critical strategic foothold on the Adriatic coast.

name: Siege of Pécs (1551)
commanders: Ottoman Empire (Sokollu Mehmed Pasha) vs. Habsburg garrison
importance: A key Ottoman offensive operation led by Sokollu Mehmed Pasha to consolidate control over the southern Hungarian border region.

name: Siege of Lippa (1551)
commanders: Habsburg (George Martinuzzi and Giovanni Battista Castaldo) vs. Ottoman garrison
importance: A significant tactical success where Christian imperial forces forced the Ottomans to abandon the city, triggering an intense Ottoman response in 1552 which led to Lippa's reoccupation.

name: Siege of Kanizsa (1543)
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg forces
importance: A failed Ottoman attempt to seize the fortress during the broad 1543 campaign season.

name: Siege of Kanizsa (1545)
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg forces
importance: Continued Habsburg resistance at this frontier post, preventing Ottoman consolidation of the region for another year.

name: Siege of Pest (1541)
commanders: Habsburg vs. Ottoman Empire
importance: Crucial defense of the city by Ottomans, which solidified their control over the Buda region.

name: Siege of Pest (1542)
commanders: Habsburg (Joachim II of Brandenburg) vs. Ottoman Empire
importance: Failed Christian attempt to retake the city; served as the catalyst for Suleiman's 1543 campaign.

name: Siege of Valpovo
commanders: Ottoman Empire (Murad Beğ Tardić) vs. Mihály Árky
importance: A key Ottoman success in Slavonia that cleared the way for the Sultan's main campaign into Hungary.

name: Siege of Pécs
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg-held Hungary
importance: Part of the systematic clearing of southern Hungarian strongholds by Suleiman the Magnificent.

name: Siege of Siklós
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg-held Hungary
importance: Secured the Ottoman flank before the march toward Székesfehérvár.

name: Siege of Székesfehérvár
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg-held Hungary
importance: The fall of the royal coronation city of the Hungarian kings was a major symbolic and strategic loss.

name: Siege of Szeged
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg-held Hungary
importance: Consolidated Ottoman power over the southern plains.

name: Battle of Szeged
commanders: Holy Roman Empire (Mihály Tóth/Bernát Aldana) vs. Ottoman Empire (Mikhaloghli Khizirbeg/Ali Hadim Pasha)
importance: The Ottoman relief army defeated the Habsburg siege forces, securing the city and demonstrating the strength of Ottoman regional garrisons.

name: Albanian Revolt (1432-1436)
commanders: Ali Bey Evrenosoglu; Gjergj Arianiti
importance: First large-scale anti-Ottoman baseline resistance, eventually put down by Rumelian army forces.

name: Capture of Krujë (Skanderbeg)
commanders: Gjergj Kastrioti (Skanderbeg); Ottoman garrison
importance: Sparked the legendary Skanderbeg Rebellion and the formation of the League of Lezhë.

name: Battle of Torvioll
commanders: Skanderbeg; Ali Pasha
importance: First massive field victory for Skanderbeg; shattered an invading Rumelian army.

name: First Battle of Mokra (1445)
commanders: Skanderbeg; Firuz Pasha
importance: Successfully repelled a secondary punitive force sent into central frontier zones.

name: Battle of Otonetë
commanders: Skanderbeg; Mustafa Pasha
importance: Defeated an invading cavalry army, protecting the territorial Integrity of central Albania.

name: Battle of Oranik (1448)
commanders: Skanderbeg; Mustafa Pasha
importance: Shattered an invading Ottoman relief army corps during the war with Venice.

name: Battle of Modrič
commanders: Skanderbeg; Hamza Kastrioti (Ottoman service)
importance: Defeated an Ottoman raiding and infiltration force within hours of contact.

name: Battle of Pollog
commanders: Skanderbeg; Ibrahim Pasha
importance: Maintained defensive perimeter stability just prior to the fall of Constantinople.

name: Battle of Berat (1455)
commanders: Isa Beg Evrenosoglu; Skanderbeg
importance: One of Skanderbeg's few major battlefield defeats, breaking the siege of the fortress.

name: Battle of Buzurshek
commanders: Skanderbeg vs. Mehmed II & Mahmud Pasha
importance: The principal engagement of Mehmed II's 1467 Albanian campaign in the Buzurshek valley near Elbasan; an Ottoman surprise night assault devastated Albanian defensive positions, resulting in massive casualties and crushing active Albanian military resistance
casualties: ~10,000 Albanian soldiers killed or captured; heavy civilian devastation

name: Battle of Albulena
commanders: Skanderbeg; Isaac Bey Evrenosoglu and Hamza Kastrioti
importance: Skanderbeg's greatest military masterpiece; completely routed a massive invading field force.

name: Second Battle of Mokra (1462)
commanders: Skanderbeg; Sinan Pasha
importance: Destroyed an invading army column, securing the central mountain passes.

name: Battle of Vaikal (1465)
commanders: Skanderbeg; Ballaban Pasha
importance: Tactical check on Ottoman advances, though several crucial Albanian commanders were captured.

name: Second Battle of Vaikal
commanders: Skanderbeg; Ballaban Pasha
importance: Ballaban Pasha was mortally wounded during the campaign, temporarily breaking the military encirclement.

name: Siege of Shkodër (1474)
commanders: Hadım Suleiman Pasha; Antonio Loredan (Venetian-Albanian garrison)
importance: Fierce defense of northern Albania; Ottoman forces withdrew due to high casualties and disease.

name: Treaty of Constantinople (1479)
commanders: Mehmed II; Venetian Republic diplomats
importance: Venice cedes Shkodër and other Albanian ports, completing the classical conquest of Albania.

name: Battle of Djerba
commanders: Piyale Pasha and Turgut Reis; Giovanni Andrea Doria (Christian Alliance)
importance: Shattered the combined Christian armada, marking the absolute high-water mark of Ottoman naval supremacy in the Mediterranean.
casualties: Heavy Christian alliance losses (half their fleet sunk/captured); minimal Ottoman losses.

name: Acquisition of the Hamid Beylik
commanders: Murad I; Kemaleddin Hüseyin Bey
importance: Expanded Ottoman control in southwestern Anatolia peacefully via purchase.

name: Union with Germiyan Beylik
commanders: Bayezid I (Marriage); Suleyman Shah of Germiyan
importance: Brought major central Anatolian territories under Ottoman control via dynastic marriage.

name: Annexation of Aydın & Saruhan
commanders: Bayezid I
importance: Unified the rich Aegean maritime principalities under direct Ottoman rule.

name: Battle of Kırkdilim
commanders: Ertuğrul Çelebi & Bayezid I vs. Kadi Burhan al-Din
importance: Fought during Bayezid I's central Anatolian campaign near Kırkdilim; court accounts claim a major victory for Kadi Burhan al-Din that checked Ottoman expansion, while contemporary accounts from vassal participants indicate a successful Ottoman raiding expedition and consolidation of territory

name: Siege of Smyrna
commanders: Timur; Knights Hospitaller defenders
importance: Timur stormed the Christian coastal fortress, dismantling the last crusader outpost in Western Anatolia.

name: Fall of Trebizond
commanders: Mehmed II; David Komnenos
importance: Annexed the Empire of Trebizond, completing complete Ottoman dominance over the Anatolian Black Sea rim.

name: Battle of Chaldiran
commanders: Selim I; Shah Ismail I (Safavid Empire)
importance: Halted Safavid western expansion, secured easternmost Anatolia, and unlocked northern Mesopotamia.

name: Battle of Turnadağ
commanders: Hadım Sinan Pasha; Bozkurt of Dulkadir
importance: Annexed the Dulkadir Beylik, ending the last independent Anatolian buffer state and completing absolute political unification.

name: Battle of Koçhisar
commanders: Bıyıklı Mehmed Pasha vs. Karahan Ustaculı
importance: Fought near Mardin and Kızıltepe during the Ottoman-Persian War; Ottoman forces led by Bıyıklı Mehmed Pasha defeated Safavid forces under Karahan Ustaculı, leading directly to the annexation of Mardin and Urfa by the Ottoman Empire
casualties: Heavy Safavid losses (estimated around 10,000 killed); light Ottoman losses (around 500)

name: Sack of Kyiv
commanders: Mengli Giray
importance: Major Crimean victory and sack of Kyiv.

name: Great Crimean Raid on Moscow
commanders: Mehmed I Giray
importance: Major raid, forces reached Moscow outskirts.

name: Battle of Sudbishchi
commanders: Devlet I Giray vs Russians
importance: Russian forces defeated Crimean raiders.

name: Burning of Moscow
commanders: Devlet I Giray
importance: Devlet Giray burns Moscow; massive enslavement.

name: Battle near Moscow
commanders: Ğazı II Giray
importance: Khan forced to retreat.

name: First Siege of Chyhyryn
commanders: Ottoman vs Russian-Cossack
importance: Russians held the fortress.

name: Chyhyryn Campaign
commanders: Kara Mustafa
importance: Chyhyryn captured and destroyed.

name: Battle of Ridaniya
commanders: Selim I vs Tuman bay II
importance: Mamluk Sultanate destroyed; Egypt annexed.

name: Chyhyryn Campaign (1674)
commanders: Grigory Romodanovsky & Ivan Samoilovich vs. Petro Doroshenko
importance: Initial joint siege and surrender of Chyhyryn to push back pro-Turkish forces in Right-bank Ukraine

name: Battle of Kaposvár
commanders: Ottoman Empire vs. Habsburg garrison
importance: Part of the Ottoman effort to neutralize Hungarian defensive fortresses south of Lake Balaton.

name: Siege of Gyula
commanders: Ottoman Empire (Pertev Pasha) vs. Habsburg garrison (László Kerecsényi)
importance: Lasting 63 days, it was the longest siege in 16th-century Hungary; its fall eliminated the last major Habsburg stronghold in eastern Hungary and secured the approaches to Transylvania.

name: Siege of Mediaș
commanders: Zápolya loyalists vs. Ferdinand I forces
importance: Part of the power struggle between John Zápolya and Ferdinand I for control over Transylvania.

name: Siege of Bihać
commanders: Ottoman Empire (Hasan-paša Predojević) vs. Habsburg garrison (Joseph Lamberg)
importance: The capture of Bihać collapsed a key defensive node in the Kingdom of Croatia, signaling the end of the relative peace and the escalation of the conflict leading into the Long Turkish War.

name: Siege of Tihany
commanders: Habsburg vs. Ottoman-aligned forces
importance: A defensive action on the Balaton frontier to prevent Ottoman-backed incursions.

name: Siege of Făgăraș
commanders: Ottoman-allied forces vs. Habsburg garrison
importance: Following the fall of Buda, this siege solidified control over the strategic approaches to Transylvania.

name: Battle of Hadad
commanders: Transylvanian forces vs. Habsburg-allied forces
importance: A key clash during the internal Hungarian civil wars that consolidated Transylvanian control in the region.

name: Siege of Krupa
commanders: Ottoman Empire (Mustafa Pasha Sokolović) vs. Habsburg garrison (Matija Bakić)
importance: A heroic defensive effort by a tiny garrison that highlights the intense pressure on the Croatian frontier prior to the full-scale Habsburg-Ottoman wars of the late 1560s.

name: Great Siege of Malta
commanders: Mustafa Pasha vs Knights Hospitaller
importance: Failed Ottoman attempt to capture Malta.

name: Battle of Wadi al-Makhazin
commanders: Ottoman-backed Saadi vs Portugal
importance: Portugal defeated; Saadi independence secured.

name: Battle of Molodi
commanders: Crimean-Ottoman vs Russia
importance: Checked northern expansion.

name: Battle of Tripoli
commanders: Turgut Reis vs Knights Hospitaller
importance: Tripoli annexed; Eyalet of Tripoli established.

name: Invasion of Calabria (1552)
commanders: Ottoman navy vs. Kingdom of Naples
importance: Part of continued Franco-Ottoman pressure on Spanish Italy

name: Capture of Corsica
commanders: Sinan Pasha & Turgut Reis (Ottoman) & Antoine Escalin des Aimars (France) vs. Genoese defenders
importance: Captured Genoese-controlled Corsica, a Spanish ally's territory

name: Evacuation/Recapture of Mahdia
commanders: Ottoman forces vs. Spanish garrison (evacuating)
importance: Spain evacuated the castle it could no longer afford to hold; Knights of Malta declined the offer to take it over

name: Siege of Oran
commanders: Hasan Pasha vs Spanish forces
importance: Major effort to expel Spanish forces from the Maghreb.

name: Siege of Mers-el-Kébir
commanders: Hasan Pasha vs Spanish forces
importance: Failed Ottoman attempt to capture the strategic presidio.

name: Battle of Molodi
commanders: Crimean-Ottoman vs Russia
importance: Checked northern expansion.

name: Capture of Tabriz (1514)
commanders: Selim I vs Safavids
importance: Ottomans entered Tabriz but later withdrew.

name: Capture of Tabriz (1534)
commanders: Suleiman I vs Safavids
importance: Ottoman occupation during Suleiman's campaign.

name: Capture of Baghdad (1534)
commanders: Suleiman I vs Safavids
importance: Baghdad permanently incorporated into the Ottoman Empire.

name: Battle of Çıldır
commanders: Lala Mustafa Pasha vs Safavids
importance: Opening the Caucasus to Ottoman advance.

name: Battle of Mollahasanli
commanders: Ottomans vs Safavids
importance: Safavid victory slowing Ottoman advance.

name: Battle of Torches
commanders: Özdemiroğlu Osman Pasha & Cafer Pasha vs. Hamza Mirza & Imam Kulu Khan
importance: Fought near Derbent (Baştepe). Famed for its intense night fighting illuminated by torches, this victory secured Ottoman control over Dagestan and Shirvan for the remainder of the war.

name: Battle of the Sunzha River
commanders: Ottomans vs Russian-Cossack forces
importance: Ottoman victory over anti-Ottoman coalition.

name: Capture of Tabriz (1585)
commanders: Ottomans vs Safavids
importance: Ottomans permanently occupied Tabriz for several years.

name: First Expedition & Siege of Caffa
